blocks.raw: <Callout>The integration subtopic is not separate content to study in addition to the others — it is the capstone that makes all the other subtopics meaningful. Every system creates coordination requirements. Every shaft, equipment room, and penetration is a negotiation between systems. Study the individual systems with the integration challenge in mind from the beginning.</Callout>

blocks.raw: <Note>The LEA frequently presents a floor plan scenario and asks you to evaluate or correct the location of an equipment room or shaft. The question is testing whether you understand the access, clearance, and system-routing requirements that make a location viable. A mechanical room on the top floor of a high-rise is unusual but sometimes correct (for cooling towers). A generator room in a basement near a flood-prone area is a design error. Know the reasoning, not just the rule.</Note>

blocks.raw: <ExamTip>The LEA has tested slab penetration coordination in scenario questions: "A plumber proposes coring a 200mm hole through a post-tensioned concrete slab to run a new sanitary drain. What is the architect's appropriate response?" The answer is that core drilling in a PT slab must be preceded by locating the PT tendons (using GPR scanning or the original structural drawings) and obtaining structural engineer approval, because severing a tendon can compromise the slab's structural integrity.</ExamTip>
